subject: Virtual machines: not a solution for now

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Virtual machines: not a solution for now
parts:
I attempted to run Vagrant, which will runs VirtualBox virtual
machines. There's a plugin that allows for Vagrant boxes to be fired
up for builds.

On the virtual machine, I ran test-unit and it took a considerable
amount longer to run the unit tests (on the range of an hour), and I
started running test-models, but stopped before finishing. I think the
speed of the virtual machine makes it a non-starter at this point. One
other complication: the plugin isn't working properly.

I'm calling it quits on trying to run virtual machines on the Jenkins
box. The question left is do we need to run automated tests on
multiple platforms? If so, does anyone know how to get a VM to run
fast and/or should we be slaving other machines and hope the
configuration is good enough?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Virtual machines: not a solution for now
parts:
On Wednesday, May 30, 2012 3:55:52 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
On the virtual machine, I ran test-unit and it took a considerable
amount longer to run the unit tests (on the range of an hour), and I
started running test-models, but stopped before finishing. I think the
speed of the virtual machine makes it a non-starter at this point.

It shouldn't be *that* slow, maybe 5 to 10% slower than native. Off the top of my head, it may be the case that the Jenkins box is too old to have hardware-assisted virtualization, or maybe it does but it has been disabled in the BIOS, or maybe it is enabled but is interfered with by Windows. Or maybe you need to increase the amount of RAM available to the VM? If the VM has to swap, then it is going to be impossibly slow. Or the 32bitness could be an issue.
One other complication: the plugin isn't working properly.
That is probably a worse problem.

I'm calling it quits on trying to run virtual machines on the Jenkins
box. The question left is do we need to run automated tests on
multiple platforms? If so, does anyone know how to get a VM to run
fast and/or should we be slaving other machines and hope the
configuration is good enough?

What are the goals here? It is primary to run test-unit with different compilers under Linux? I'd still say that Hotfoot is best suited for this, but we might have to work with the sysadmins. AFAIK, the jobs are farmed out to virtual machines on Hotfoot, so it is certainly possible to do computationally intensive stuff without that much of a performance penalty.

Ben

On Thursday, August 16, 2012 6:31:24 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'm going to lead with the issue that's bugging me and then
get to Ben's post on Windows 8.

How much of the following space do we want to test and support:

    OS version  x  bit size  x  compiler  x  library version

At some point, we just have to let users be our testers, and if Stan doesn't work for some combination of the above that users might have, they know where to find us. That said, there is a lot of value for us to be able to say on the website that the following combinations passed our unit tests (and possibly model tests) on $DATE. That would encourage users with the same or similar combinations to download Stan and find out whether that still holds.

(Tangent: Perhaps the binary version(s) of Stan could come with a testme executable?)

And all that said, we have been really, really lucky or good in the sense that we haven't had a major compilation problem on any attempted OS, bitness, compiler version, and library version since Jenkins got Rtools, and I believe we did it without a single ifdef hack in the Stan code.
Here's what I know about:

In addition, you have Sun / Oracle hardware (where Stan will probably work with a recent g++ but definitely not with the Sun / Oracle compiler), various *BSD systems (where Stan will probably work if it works on a Mac), and in the near-future, if not already, ARM-based tablets (where Stan could work but likely does not at the moment).
Is it possible to set up virtual machines to do all this?
Yes, although the Apple Cops might seize any non-Apple hardware that was running a virtualized Apple OS.
How do we create a VM and which hardware/OS do we need?

I think any hardware / OS combination is fine, except the aforementioned non-Apple / Apple one and 32bit native hardware / 64bit OS. A VM program like

https://www.virtualbox.org/

allows you to create a VM from either a physical CD / DVD that installs the OS or an .iso file of said CD / DVD.

Ben
